name: VeriCrypt
tagline: An engine that inventories the cryptography in an estate, flags quantum-vulnerable assets, and produces signed reports anyone can verify offline.

audience.concern: Know which cryptography is exposed to quantum attack, what to fix first, and how to show regulators.
Verify a compliance report offline, without trusting the vendor or the institution.
Run the engine on your own machines from one binary and keep the report and signing key under your control.

highlights.title: Finds and classifies cryptography
highlights.text: Reads certificates and keys from folders and probes TLS endpoints. RSA, EC and Ed25519 keys are classified as quantum-vulnerable or resistant, and findings fire on real properties such as weak keys, SHA-1 signatures and plaintext private keys.

highlights.title: Dated against standards
highlights.text: Applies NIST IR 8547 (draft) transition years and the CA/Browser Forum certificate-lifetime schedule to forecast what will need replacing.

highlights.title: Signed, tamper-evident reports
highlights.text: Reports are signed with SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128f (the FIPS 205 algorithm) and carry a Merkle root. Editing a report is detected, and a report with no signature fails verification.

highlights.title: Machine-readable inventory
highlights.text: Produces a CycloneDX 1.7 cryptographic bill of materials that validates against the official schema, plus an HTML report.

highlights.title: Built for gates
highlights.text: A diff command compares two scans, and a fail-on threshold returns an exit code your pipeline can act on.

verifyIt: Run vericrypt verify on a report with the signer's public key pinned. Then edit the report and verify again: verification fails.

demo.title: Verify a signed report
demo.summary: Check a report, then tamper with it and see verification fail. The in-browser verifier is planned; this page shows a labeled placeholder until it ships.

status: v2 evidence engine built and tested; later versions in design

buildFromSource.title: Build from source
buildFromSource.intro: VeriCrypt has no packaged binaries yet. Build it from source (about 15 minutes the first time).
buildFromSource.steps:
git clone https://github.com/DamainRamsajan/vericrypt.git
cd vericrypt
cargo build --release -p vericrypt
./target/release/vericrypt --help
buildFromSource.note: Needs Rust and OpenSSL headers. Do not run cargo update: the lock file pins a dependency the signing library needs.

faq.q: The build fails with 'linker cc not found'.
faq.a: Install the build tools: on Ubuntu or Debian, sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libssl-dev clang.

faq.q: The build fails mentioning signature or slh_dsa.
faq.a: You probably ran cargo update. Restore Cargo.lock; it pins signature 2.3.0-pre.4 because newer pre-releases break the signing library.

faq.q: Why does 'vericrypt scan' print a warning?
faq.a: That is the old v1 command and is deprecated. Use vericrypt analyze.

faq.q: Does it run on macOS, Windows or ARM?
faq.a: Only Ubuntu 24.04 (and WSL2) has been tested. macOS, native Windows and ARM are untested.

faq.q: Is the report a compliance certification?
faq.a: No. VeriCrypt produces an observation-based inventory and findings. It does not certify compliance.
